newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end narrowly mixed, PGMs lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end narrowly mixed, PGMs lower.

text.p: Tokyo gold futures ended mixed on Tuesday, shrugging off remarks by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that Japan had in the past been tempted to sell U.S. Treasuries and switch foreign reserves to gold, traders said.
Platinum group metals (PGM) ended mostly lower on fresh selling although there were no signs yet that Russia has resumed PGM sales in the spot market.
Gold futures ranged from five yen per gram lower to four yen up. Benchmark April closed one yen weaker at 1,243 yen.
"In gold futures, private investors were quick to take advantage of any price rebound to sell gold as sentiment in gold remains bearish," one analyst at a commodity broker said.
The yen's slight recovery against the dollar undermined market sentiment, the traders said.
Spot gold was quoted at $339.15/65 per ounce at 0731 GMT, against $339.10/60 in New York on Monday.

In palladium futures, four distant months temporarily fell by their 22 yen per gram daily limit before the close, amid growing expectations that Russia would resume PGM exports later this week, traders said.

"Even if Russia resumes PGM exports soon, the Japanese palladium market supply/demand situation has been seriously disrupted by the protracted suspension of Russian sales. This will limit falls in PGMs, especially palladium," a trader said.
Palladium futures ranged from 22 yen per gram lower to four yen up. Benchmark April was off 18 yen at 507 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from four to 25 yen per gram lower, with benchmark April off four yen at 1,355 yen.
Silver futures were firmer on the back of stronger spot silver prices. Benchmark April silver was up 1.4 yen per 10 grams at 178.6 yen. --Tokyo Commodities Desk -81-3-3432-7431
